input.lyrics:
I remember the feeling,
warm but uneasy,
new home, new city,
low self-esteem.
I took pill after pill
just to quiet my head,
then smoked by the window
and stayed in my bed.
Dropped acid alone while
the ceiling turned strange
and waited for something
inside me to change.
My dealer knew
when I needed a spark,
and I called that friendship
because it was enough.
At sixteen, I thought
I had years left to lose.
At seventeen,
I had habits to choose.
I don't miss the fear
or the things I went through.
I miss being young enough
not to know what they'd do.
My first love came
through that apartment door.
I had never let anyone
that close before.
I kept the opioids
hidden where nobody would see,
took more than I intended
and kept it all with me.
I overdosed in silence
with the bedroom door shut tight,
then woke up hours later
and said that I was alright.
I didn't know what was wrong
or why I hated my skin.
I only knew the pills could cut
the pressure down within.
I don't call it good,
and I don't call it bad.
It held some of the worst
and the best that I had.
Now when I remember,
I can't make it clean.
I hated those years,
but I still miss sixteen.
Newark is traffic
I pass on the way,
but part of me stays
in that bedroom some days.
I wasn't chasing
a story to tell.
I don't miss that bedroom,
at least not completely,
but sometimes I miss
what it meant to be sixteen.
I remember the feeling,
warm but uneasy,
a new home, a new city,
a life in between.
